title: Dressing Up Around the World
strapline: Wrap a sari, tie a headwrap, slip on a kimono — try the world on for size.
intent: Exploring clothes worn by people around the world helps children value the many ways people dress and celebrate.
Wrapping, tying, fastening and draping real fabrics is rich fine-motor and self-care practice.
Trying on clothes from different cultures sparks imaginative role-play and stories.
Talking about what their own family wears, especially for celebrations, honours each child's heritage.
The theme grows respect: different clothes are beautiful and special, never strange.
implementation: Offer a dressing-up collection with clothes and fabrics from many cultures — a sari length, a headwrap, a kimono, kente cloth, hats and shoes.
Show children how some are worn — wrapping and tying — and let them practise the fastenings and drapes.
Wonder together respectfully: 'This is worn for special celebrations — I wonder what it feels like to wear.'
Invite families to lend or show an outfit worn for a celebration, and treat each with care and pride.
Feed in the self-care too — buttons, ties, wraps — the fine-motor work of dressing.
Follow the play — some children will dress and parade, others will build whole stories around their outfits.
key_questions: How do you think this is worn — shall we try wrapping it?
What does your family wear for a special day or celebration?
How does this fabric feel — soft, shiny, heavy?
Can you fasten this on your own, or shall we do it together?
What story could you play, dressed like this?

impact.text: Children wrap, tie and fasten real clothing, practising dressing and self-care.
Children talk about their own family's clothes and notice others dress differently.
Children show respect for clothes and celebrations different from their own.
Children use the dressing-up in imaginative role-play and stories.
Children explore how different fabrics look and feel.

enhancements: A world dressing-up rail with saris, headwraps, kimonos, kente cloth, hats and shoes.
A mirror and a 'catwalk' for parading and looking at outfits.
A family-lent celebration outfit, shown and handled with care.
A fabric-feeling basket to explore textures and patterns.
A wrapping-and-tying practice station for the fine-motor work of dressing.

playing_exploring: Children try on, wrap and drape, exploring clothes from around the world.
They handle fabrics and fastenings with hands-on curiosity.
active_learning: Children persist with a tricky wrap or tie until it holds.
They build and sustain role-play around their outfits.
creating_thinking: Children work out how a garment is worn and fastened.
They connect clothes to families, celebrations and their own experience.
